records.detail: The Central Bank of Seychelles' Report on International Reserves Management 2025 says a small portion of its Australian dollar reserves was maintained with the BIS; the report does not describe the BIS as a manager or custodian, only as the institution with which the currency was held.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Seychelles, Report on International Reserves Management (Reserves Management Annual Report 2025)
records.quote: a small portion of the currency was maintained with the Bank for International Settlements (BIS)

records.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
records.detail: The Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador's own document on international reserves management states that the BCR joined the World Bank's RAMP reserve-management advisory programme in 2010; the document describes RAMP as advice on reserve management, not as managing a portfolio, and it names no external portfolio manager or custodian, referring only generically to 'administradores externos de portafolios de inversion'.
records.as_of: 2010 (joined); document current as of its publication
records.source_title: Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador, La Gestion de las Reservas Internacionales
records.quote: Programa de Asesoria sobre Gestion de Reservas (RAMP, por sus siglas en ingles) del Banco Mundial

records.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
records.detail: The National Bank of Moldova's own page on external technical cooperation states that the World Bank assists the NBM through the Reserve Advisory and Management Program (RAMP), described as technical assistance to improve management of the state's foreign exchange reserves and knowledge sharing among member states; the page names no external portfolio manager and does not say RAMP manages any portfolio.
records.source_title: National Bank of Moldova, External Technical Cooperation
records.quote: The World Bank assists the NBM in the Reserve Advisory and Management Program (RAMP).

not_found.note: Opened World Bank press release 15 Apr 2026 welcoming the Central Bank of Ecuador to RAMP (the 25th-anniversary release). It names NO other member: only Ecuador, which is already on the row. States 'RAMP has reached a record 95 members' and that RAMP 'delivers advisory services, executive training, and asset management solutions'; it does not say RAMP manages Ecuador's portfolio.

Opened World Bank press release 16 Apr 2026 on Kosovo's new phase. Names only the CBK, already on the row twice, so not duplicated. Worth passing to the map owner as an upgrade of the existing Kosovo record: 'Beginning this year, a portion of the CBK's reserves will be managed by RAMP' - i.e. actual portfolio management, not just membership. Also: CBK was 'the first institution to join RAMP through the Trust Fund for Public Asset Management in 2023' and the first to move from trust-fund to asset-mandate membership. Release says RAMP 'has advised over 100 public institutions'.

Opened the RAMP programme page (treasury.worldbank.org) and the RAMP 'Global Network' page. Neither publishes a member list. Between them they name as member institutions only: Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago, Bank of Guatemala, National Bank of Cambodia, Bulgarian National Bank, Central Bank of Cabo Verde, Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Central Bank of the Republic of Armenia, Central Bank of Ecuador - all already on the row - plus three non-central-bank members (Korea National Pension Service, Panama Savings Fund, Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN) and the Pension Agency of Georgia. Bank of Korea and Central Bank of Chile appear only as event co-hosts, which is not membership, so not recorded. No total count on the Global Network page.

Opened the World Bank Treasury blog 'Serving public asset managers globally' and Central Banking's 'Two decades of investing in reserve managers'. Neither names a central bank member: Central Banking says only that RAMP 'serves more than 70 members' and that the first member, in October 2001, was an unnamed 'European central bank'.

Opened the ECCB Annual Report 2025-2026 in three passes covering the financial statements and all notes. CONFIRMS the brief: the external managers and custodian are still unnamed. Note 3(b) says 'The activities of the global custodian are also monitored daily and their overall performance is periodically reviewed' and note 3(a) refers to 'Performance of the external fund money managers and the internal fund manager' - no firm anywhere. Bank of America appears only as the destination to which currency notes are shipped.

Opened the BCR's own document 'La Gestion de las Reservas Internacionales'. Yielded the RAMP record filed above (joined 2010, advisory). The BCR names NO external portfolio manager or custodian: it refers generically to 'administradores externos de portafolios de inversion' and has an 'Administradores Externos' box on its org chart, and sets size criteria for 'Bancos Custodios' without naming one. Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) appears only as the publisher of its benchmark indices, not as a manager. So El Salvador is a new confirmed-external-managers-but-unnamed case. The BCR homepage 'Gestion de Reservas' carries nothing.

Opened Banco de la Republica's 'Estadisticas de las Reservas Internacionales'. Colombia's external-manager programme runs about 30% of reserves - 'El programa de administradores externos gestiona aproximadamente el 30 % de los recursos' - but the firms are described only as 'firmas especializadas en portafolios de inversion' and no custodian is mentioned. A new known blank: confirmed external managers, none named. Amundi is already on the row for Colombia.

Opened the Central Bank of Seychelles Reserves Management Annual Report 2025. Confirms the three parties already on the row (Crown Agents Investment Management, UBS money market fund, RAMP) and adds the BIS holding a small portion of AUD reserves, filed above with the source's own wording. No global custodian is named - the report mentions 'settlement and custodian relationships' only as a staff-training topic.

Opened the Bank of Israel 'Investment of the Foreign Exchange Reserves' annual report. It confirms external managers are used - 'The investment is executed by internal and external investment managers' - but names none. Moody's and Bloomberg appear only as rating and data sources. BlackRock is already on the row for Israel.

Opened the Reserve Bank of Fiji Annual Report Aug 2023-Jul 2024 (first pass, report is long). No external manager or custodian named; it states 'The Reserve Bank of Fiji holds and manages the country's foreign reserves as delegated under the RBF Act (1983)'. Did not read past the first 100,000 characters.

Opened the National Reserve Bank of Tonga Annual Report 2017 (first pass). No external manager or custodian named; reserves held with unnamed banks rated above a Board-approved 'A' minimum. Only outside bodies named are the IMF (technical assistance to review reserves management) and PricewaterhouseCoopers (external auditor). Did not read past the first 100,000 characters.

Opened the Central Bank of The Bahamas Annual Report and Statement of Accounts 2024 (first pass). The Foreign Reserves Management section names no external manager or custodian; the Bahamas Depositary Receipts programme refers only to 'three active broker-dealers'. Budget ran out before the financial-statement notes could be read - worth a second pass at offset 100000.

Not researched further, but noted for the known-blanks list: a Business Standard report quotes then-governor Shaktikanta Das saying the RBI engages an external manager for a very small part of FX reserves, for learning purposes, with no firm named. Confirmed external manager, firm unnamed.

Supplier-side route tried and failed: Crown Agents Investment Management's own history page says 'We work with over 30 central banks globally' but names none, so no client list is available there. Searches for firm-named mandates (State Street, Goldman Sachs AM, JPMorgan AM, Northern Trust, BlackRock, Amundi, Pictet) returned only the managers' own fund accounts, not central bank mandates. The World Bank RAMP Reserve Management Survey reports (2019, 2021, 2023, 2025 editions) and OMFIF's Global Public Investor remain anonymised, as the brief says.
